newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks surge to new highs on stable U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks surge to new highs on stable U.S. rates.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks surged in early Wednesday trade, with the Hang Seng Index rising 155 points, or 1.09 percent, to a record high of 14,391 after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to leave interest rates unchanged.
"The rally is mainly due to the interest rate news and sentiment is bullish since there is no bad news heard so far," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"Volume should improve today with a bit of profit-taking across the board."
After an initial burst to a record high of 14,398.55, the blue-chip index retreated to 14,312, up 76 points or 0.54 percent.
Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said the index was likely to move below resistance at 14,400 on Wednesday.
